items.note: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 — all four present in story 1.
Article VII given as paid by the butterfat test of the station where delivered, not by weight of milk — both bolded halves present.
Never states that Article VII is what made a wrong test cost money; only quotes 'the hinge of the whole matter'. The nearest statement is in Section B, which cannot travel into A.
Only Hobart Sill (buttermaker, Larrow Green) appears. Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from Section A; one of three officers is not the item's core fact.
Selby Vose absent from Section A entirely. Section B has him as Gideon's son but manager 'from 1911' (wrong year), and B cannot travel into A.
The 'station gain' ledger line appears only at C1(a). Credit never travels into Section A from B–G.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glassware lent from Larrow Green (Sill's) — all bolded elements present.
No description of the bench system: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read off the graduated neck after a fixed pipette charge, no cream-out/skim-back.
Ammon & Sons, invoice of 14 April 1897, outfit in use from 1 May 1897. 'Tarnet' not named, but the firm and both dates carry the core fact.
Invoice contents listed, but the pipettes' marked 17.6 c.c. is nowhere in the sheet, and the total is left as an unresolved $77.93/$77.39 pair rather than settled at $77.93.
Flatness of the 0.19 shortfall across every month and all twenty-six years is stated only at C1(b), in Section C.
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that no burette existed in the county.
Ansel Keddie, tester at Ostrey Hollow from 1896, twenty-nine unbroken seasons, service ending 1925. Exact dismissal date (30 April) missing but the service and its end are given.
Thin credit on the bold mechanic: the test book is named as Keddie's own record, kept across the twenty-nine seasons. None of the unbolded detail (columns, corrections crossed and initialed) appears.
The summary leaf is absent from Section A; neither 3.80 for 1896 nor 3.61 from 1898 appears there. Both figures are required and both sit only in Section C.
8 May 1911 breakage, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests up through the interval and straight back down on return, and Keddie's question mark. Only the 3.80 level is missing.
Orra appears in Section A only as 'the tester's own wife' with a diary. No Orra Brant, no sister of Emmet Brant, no largest-patron link. The B2 discussion cannot travel into A.
Section A mentions 1919 only as the year the 1908 finding stopped holding. No water circular over the manager's signature, and no Keddie statement of 17 March 1925.
No death in 1934 under the imputation, no impounding of the test book, no county historical rooms in 1959.
Granddaughter, stated flatly and correctly.

No kinship chain. The sheet resolves great-niece vs granddaughter by the author's own signed correction but explicitly denies the derivation the key requires — at B2 it says 'no source names which of Ansel's children is Ivy's parent'.
Reaches second cousins with the Roy/Duncan first-cousin step laid out, hedged as 'most likely'. Hedging is not an error and the answer is right.

Abstention item A08 (full vs half siblings of Emmet and Orra) is never raised. The sheet declines a different question — whether Orra is Emmet's sister at all. No assertion either, so no gullibility deduction.
Gideon Vose, father, with the nephew claim named and rejected.
Credited under the B–G scope rule from B4: Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's own test the basis of payment, and his son signed the 1919 circular accusing those same patrons.
Correct abstention. Verdict sentence is source-framed ('none that the sources establish'), and it closes 'cannot be determined from the sources'. No assertion of kinship or of its absence.

States the institutional link instead of the evidentiary position the key wants: two narrators asserting a cousinship from talk, one flat denial, no document either way, a family member's denial not being a record. None of that appears.

Answers 5.25 percent (station-gain ledger note) instead of 0.95 / 5 percent short. Never computes 16.72 ÷ 17.6, and explicitly declines to get the figure from the glassware, which is what the question asks.
True average 3.80, recorded short by 0.19 of a point.
76,000 lb, with 40,000,000 × 0.19 percent shown.

Headline answer is $19,600 and 19.4 percent — exactly the NT-8 cascade. The key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth; both are required and both are wrong. The correct $19,000 appears only as a flagged discrepancy it decides against.
Declined. C2 is not an abstention item: the sources identify Emmet Brant as the largest patron and give 200,000 lb at 3.42 for 1910. Answer is 6,840 lb.
Declined. Answer is 360 lb (7,200 true less 6,840 credited).
Declined. Answer is $86.40.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: 'Selby Vose became the Association's manager in 1911' (B3, repeated in B4). Correct year is 1913; 1911 is catalogued as a planted error. Charged once.
Planted error asserted as fact: the loss put at $19,600 (F081) at C1(d), adopted as 'Bulletin 471's own computed figure' over the correct $19,000.
